title: ready-07: extension services on the server — what heca-pro mounts its services on
summary: A public, generic way for an extension to run a service inside the heca server (daemon and standalone), with its own lifecycle, context, wakeup, client projection and action access.
description:
Requested by heca-pro (Heca-Pro P003(F001)/T013, also consumed by T014). Proposed contract: `~/projects/heca-pro-feat-13/docs/open-heca-work.md:40` ("Server service contract for T013"). heca owns the generic mounting, lifecycle, wakeup, action context and client projection; heca-pro owns its service implementation, room logic and archive. heca must stay generic: no heca-pro room or conversation types in heca.

## Current state (verified on main a5dd334d, 2026-11-14)
- The public extension entry point `heca::extension(name)` (`heca/src/entry/extension.rs:44`) offers only actions (`:80`), layers (`:87`), terminals (`:105`) and pane contributions (`pane_button`, `pane_chip`, `pane_line`). There is no server-side service.
- An extension action handler is `Fn(&mut ProviderCx, &Intent) -> Handled` (`heca/src/entry/action.rs:45`; `ProviderCx` at `heca/src/providers/mod.rs:230`). It reads the chrome store and emits intents; it cannot reach server state or a service.
- The headless server `serve()` (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs:7`) builds the `ServerLoop` and calls `register_extensions` (`heca/src/server/run/mod.rs:101`), which registers only queued actions (`entry/action.rs:110`).
- Nothing server-side is publicly exported from `heca/src/lib.rs`.

## Reusable building blocks (internal today)
- Waking the owner loop from another thread and submitting work: the notification sink does exactly this (`headless.rs:14` `install_notification_sink` → `RuntimeHandle::raise` → `Event::Notification`; `heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs:17` `Event`, `:29` `RuntimeHandle`, `:142` `dispatch`).
- Per-topic projections sent to attached clients on attach and on change: `publish_notifications` / `publish_windows` (`heca/src/server/session/publish.rs:96`, `:72`), and the script event stream `StreamEvent` / `EventFanout` (`heca/src/server/events.rs:22`, `:37`, T546).
- Identities: `heca_core::layout::SessionId` (public) and `Connection.id` (`heca/src/server/connection.rs:19`, internal; the one window identity, decision 2534270c).
- Wire vocabulary: `ClientMsg` / `ServerMsg` (`heca/src/server/wire/mod.rs:35`, `:93`).

## Behaviour to provide (from the heca-pro contract, to be agreed first)
1. A builder-style extension declaration registers a service factory before `heca::run()`. The host invokes it once per actual server (daemon and standalone), never per window, dock, session switch or snapshot.
2. Lifecycle without a window, winit or GPU; closing a client does not stop it; server shutdown stops it once, with bounded queues and visible failures.
3. A public context with the configuration/path owner and the real server/session/client identities (reuse `SessionId` and `Connection.id`; no second window identity; a request never asserts its sender).
4. Background work wakes the loop and submits bounded results without polling or blocking dispatch; service data is committed before the projection event that announces it.
5. The existing transport carries an initial extension snapshot plus versioned deltas to permitted clients; reattach or a lost/expired cursor gets a fresh snapshot; a client is never the authority.
6. Registered actions reach their owning service through public context; native UI, RPC and other commands keep the existing action/permission/result door. No second server, private dispatcher or terminal-input injection.

## Rules
AGENTS.md § 0 and Rule Zero: the API is what a plugin author types (builder on the extension, no registry lookups, ids or crate-private types in authoring). Reuse the wakeup, projection and identity mechanisms above instead of a parallel path. Work in its own worktree; the shape is agreed with heca-pro before code.

Depends on: P104 (server/client split), P099 (socket, events), P100 (sessions) — all in place.

tasks.title: Extension services on the server: mount, lifecycle, context, wakeup, client projection, action access
tasks.description:
One generic capability for heca-pro (and any extension): run a service inside the heca server. Full context, code references and the requested behaviour are in the phase P108(F012) description; the heca-pro proposal is `~/projects/heca-pro-feat-13/docs/open-heca-work.md:40`.

What exists vs what to build:
- Exists: extension entry point with actions/layers/terminals/pane contributions (`heca/src/entry/extension.rs:44`); action handlers get `ProviderCx` only (`heca/src/entry/action.rs:45`); `ServerLoop::register_extensions` registers actions only (`heca/src/server/run/mod.rs:101`); the headless entry (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs:7`); internal wakeup via `RuntimeHandle` (`heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs:29`), already used by notifications (`headless.rs:14`); per-topic client projections (`heca/src/server/session/publish.rs:72`, `:96`) and the event stream (`heca/src/server/events.rs`).
- To build: a public service declaration on the extension builder, a host-owned lifecycle per server, a public service context, a supported wakeup/submit path, a generic versioned snapshot+delta projection to clients over the existing `ClientMsg`/`ServerMsg` transport, and action access to the owning service.

Steps are the checklist. Step 1 (agree the API shape with the heca-pro agent) comes before any code; record the agreed shape as an Accepted Decision on this task.

Edge cases to cover: daemon vs standalone (one invocation per server, not per window); several servers in one process get separate service instances; client detach/reattach and session switch never restart the service; lost or expired cursor → fresh snapshot; server shutdown stops workers once; a failing factory is reported visibly and does not take the server down silently; no heca-pro types in heca.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped on branch feat/t553-extension-services (worktree heca-feat-553), following decision c7fb5fc3.

Authoring API, in heca/src/entry/service/:
- `ext.service(short, factory) -> ServiceRegistration<S>`, plus the trait `Service` (receive / project / stop, `SCHEMA_VERSION`).
- `registration.action(meta, handler)`, where the handler receives `&mut S` and returns `ActionResult::{Done, Refused, Later(ticket)}`.
- `registration.client(initial, apply) -> ServiceState<C>`, a reactive value on the window.
- `ServiceInbox` is bounded and Send, and a send wakes the server through the RuntimeHandle waker.
- Contexts: `StartCx`, `ServiceCx` (republish, complete), `ActionCx` (session, optional client, effective session config, later), `ProjectCx` (session, client, config, epoch, since).

Host, in heca/src/server/services/:
- Started in `ServerLoop::from_config`, so once per server, for both the daemon and standalone. Two servers in one process each start their own.
- Each pump drains the inboxes.
- Projections are computed per window (session plus connection), with per-window revisions and a server epoch. A window gets a snapshot on attach, on reattach, on `ClientMsg::ServiceResync`, and when it holds data from another server run. Updates are checked against `max_frame_bytes`.
- Wire messages: `ServerMsg::Service` and `ClientMsg::ServiceResync`.
- Deferred tickets keep the RPC reply until the service settles them; a window is told only about a refusal.
- `shutdown` calls stop until Done, delivering inbox messages in between, within `stop_timeout_ms`, then answers the callers still waiting. The daemon loop end now calls `shutdown`.
- A failing factory, message or projection is reported as a notification plus a line on stderr. Start-up reports are held for the first session.

Routing:
- Service action metadata enters the one catalog through `register_queued_actions`, as `DynamicHandler::Service`. A name already taken is refused and reported.
- A window's call goes `ClientMsg::Invoke` → session → host.
- A script's direct call goes `begin_rpc` → `rpc_service`, using the shared check `check_server_intent` extracted from `execute_server_with`.
- A script chain that ends in a service action now works too: `execute_server_with` hands its callers a `ServerStep::{Action, Service}`.

Settings: `[settings.services] inbox_capacity = 256, stop_timeout_ms = 3000` (config.default.toml, heca-config/src/settings/services.rs). `StartupQueue` gained `close` / `is_closed` / `peek`, so every server reads the service declarations.

Docs:
- docs/extending-heca.md, section "A service inside the server".
- docs/server-client-architecture.md, section "Extension services".

Verification:
- Unit tests: 5 in entry/service/tests.rs and 9 in server/run/service_tests.rs. They cover:
  - one instance per server, never restarted by detach or reattach;
  - snapshot, then delta, then reattach or resync giving a snapshot;
  - a script answered at once, deferred, or with "who asked";
  - a window's call, with a refusal shown;
  - shutdown waiting for a pending stop, and stopping once;
  - a failing factory;
  - an update over the frame limit;
  - the owner loop waking for a worker's message and stopping its services at the end;
  - a script chain ending in a service action.
- Each guarded behaviour was broken on purpose and its test went red. A guard that could not be caught was redundant, so it was removed.
- `cargo test -p heca -p heca-config`: all pass, 1220 heca lib tests.
- Clippy on toolchain 1.100.0 with a forced re-lint: clean. `cargo doc --document-private-items` for heca: clean.
- Not verified: no GUI run. A component reading `ServiceState` in the real app has not been tried; there is no GUI change.

acceptedDecisions.title: Server extension services: agreed contract with heca-pro (factory + typed service + registration-bound actions)
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed on 2026-11-14 between heca (Opus) and the heca-pro agent, relayed and approved by Antonio. Shape: `ext.service(name, factory)` registers a factory run once per actual server (daemon and standalone, never per window/dock/session switch/snapshot), returning a `ServiceRegistration<S>`; actions are declared on that registration and receive `&mut S` directly (no plugin-written lookups).
1. Threads: no Send/Sync on the factory or the service — registrations are thread-local and the server loop runs on the registering thread. Only the service inbox and its messages cross threads.
2. Stop: `stop(cx) -> Done | Pending`, non-blocking, safe to call repeatedly, with a shutdown deadline from config.
3. Context: a new per-run server identity (epoch); the session's effective configuration is available to actions and projections. heca-pro's persistent archive identity stays separate and is not heca's concern.
4. Identity: only the provenance heca really has — the session and an optional `Connection.id` (absent for windowless RPC). No promise of authentication.
5. Projection: computed by the service per recipient (session + client). `None` removes that recipient's previous projection; it does not mean "no update". Payload is serializable (JSON on the wire), with service, schema_version, server_epoch, revision, base_revision (absent for snapshots), kind snapshot|delta; attach, reconnect, different epoch or a missing revision force a snapshot; size bounds; only committed data.
6. Client: the extension applies snapshots and deltas (it knows their meaning). heca owns transport, revision checking, snapshot re-requests and public reactive access from components — no manual lookups or per-dock state copies.
7. Actions: the existing action path (`ClientMsg::Invoke` → server-side dynamic actions, same catalog/permission/RPC door), returning either an immediate result or a deferred ticket the service completes after commit. A timeout or disconnect never re-runs the action nor implicitly cancels an accepted transaction.
8. Names: `<extension>.<action>`; duplicates are refused with a visible error.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: heca-pro needs a server-resident service (rooms) built on open heca. The corrected contract matches what heca really has: thread-local registration on the owner thread, ServerWaker-based wakeup, JSON wire, per-recipient projections (as per-window notifications), the existing server-side dynamic action path, local owner-only identity. It keeps heca generic and the authoring API Rule-Zero compliant.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Reuse: RuntimeHandle/Event wakeup used by the notification sink (heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs, headless.rs:14) for the bounded service inbox; per-recipient projection like `visible_notifications_for`; `ClientMsg::Invoke` → `execute_server_dynamic` (heca/src/server/session/mod.rs:366, heca/src/actions/registry/mod.rs:188) for actions; `<extension>.<short>` naming and the existing duplicate refusal. New: server epoch; deferred correlated replies (today RPC answers are synchronous with a timeout, heca/src/server/socket/runtime.rs:89); a generic versioned extension projection message in ClientMsg/ServerMsg; a client-side public reactive accessor fed by the extension's snapshot/delta appliers; per-service inbox bounds and shutdown deadline as config keys. Still to fix exact signatures during implementation: how the service signals "republish" (e.g. after commit) so heca recomputes per-recipient projections, and the client-side accessor/applier declaration on the registration.

checklist.title: Agree the public API shape with the heca-pro agent (service declaration, context, wakeup, projection, action access); record it as an Accepted Decision

Service declaration on the extension builder + host-owned lifecycle: created once per server (daemon and standalone), unaffected by clients/session switches, stopped once on shutdown with visible failures
Public service context: configuration/path owner and real server/session/client identities (reuse SessionId and Connection.id; no second window identity; requests never assert their sender)
Wakeup and bounded result submission from background work, reusing the RuntimeHandle path the notification sink uses; data committed before its projection event

Generic extension projection: initial snapshot + versioned deltas to permitted clients over the existing ClientMsg/ServerMsg transport; fresh snapshot on reattach or lost cursor; clients never authoritative
Registered actions reach their owning service through public context, through the existing action/permission/result door (UI, RPC)
Tests (daemon + standalone, reattach, shutdown, multiple servers) and docs (docs/server-client-architecture.md + the extension authoring guide)

tasks.title: Extension services: persistent data folder and the extension's own configuration
tasks.description:
Requested by heca-pro (T013 is integrating T553 and is blocked on this), approved by Antonio on 2026-11-14. It extends the T553 contract, decision c7fb5fc3; the extension is recorded as a decision on this task.

## What exists
- `StartCx` (heca/src/entry/service/cx.rs) gives `config()`, `server_epoch()` and `inbox()`. It has no persistent path.
- The epoch changes on every start (heca/src/server/services/mod.rs `new_epoch`).
- heca's data folder is `heca_config::state_file::data_path(file)` (heca-config/src/state_file.rs), which resolves to `dirs::data_dir()/heca/<file>`.
- No server has a stable name. The socket is always `default.sock` (heca/src/server/socket/mod.rs `socket_path`).
- The server is started by `ServerLoop::from_config` (heca/src/server/bootstrap.rs) → `start_services` → `ServiceHost::start(config, wake)`. It is reached from the daemon (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs` `serve`) and from standalone (`heca/src/client/local.rs` `LocalServer::new`).
- `Config` (heca-config/src/loader/mod.rs `struct Config`) has only heca's own fields. An unknown table such as `[extensions.x]` is dropped.
- Configuration layering: embedded defaults → user `config.toml` → trusted project `.heca/config.toml`.
- A session's effective config is in `SessionRuntime::config()` and reaches actions through `ActionCx::config()`.

## To build
1. **`StartCx::data_dir() -> &Path`.** The folder owned by this service on this server: `<data dir>/heca/servers/<server name>/<extension>.<service>/`.
   - The server name is `default` for the background server (`heca --server`) and `standalone` for a standalone window. It is passed into `ServerLoop::from_config` by each entry point; it is not guessed.
   - heca creates the folder owner-only (0700) before calling the factory.
   - It stays stable across restarts, unlike the epoch.
   - If the platform has no data folder, the factory gets an error reported like any factory failure; it never panics.
   - Also exposed on `ServiceCx`/`ActionCx` if cheap, so a service need not store it itself.
2. **`[extensions.<name>]` in config.**
   - `Config` keeps a generic `extensions: toml::Table` (no heca-pro fields), merged per key through the same layering.
   - `extension_config::<T: DeserializeOwned>() -> Result<T, _>` on `StartCx` reads the server config, and on `ActionCx`/`ProjectCx` reads the session's effective config.
   - The extension name comes from the service registration (`<extension>.<service>` → `<extension>`), so one extension can never read another's table.
   - A missing table deserializes from an empty table, so `#[serde(default)]` types work.
   - A config reload (`ClientMsg::Reload` → `SessionRuntime::reload_config`) refreshes what actions and projections see.
3. **Docs.** docs/extending-heca.md, section "A service inside the server": data_dir and extension_config, plus an example `[extensions.demo]` block. README/config.default.toml: document that `[extensions.<name>]` exists.

## Edge cases
- A refused or late service gets no folder.
- Two servers in one process with the same name share the folder: tests must use a temp data root, never the user's real folder (inject the root).
- Never put heca-pro names in heca.

acceptedDecisions.title: Service data folder per server + service; extension config typed from [extensions.<name>]
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed on 2026-11-14 by Antonio and the heca-pro agent. This extends T553 decision c7fb5fc3.
1. `StartCx::data_dir() -> &Path` returns the folder that belongs to this server and this service, in `<data dir>/heca/servers/<server>/<extension>.<service>/`. heca creates it owner-only before the factory runs. It stays the same across restarts, unlike the epoch, and is separate from every other service's folder.
2. Server naming:
   - The background server is `default`.
   - `standalone` is only a category. Two standalone windows running at the same time must never open the same archive. Each standalone server therefore claims the lowest free slot, `standalone-1`, `standalone-2` and so on, by taking an exclusive lock on it for its whole life. A restarted standalone gets its slot back, so its folder is stable.
   - The background server takes the same lock on `default`.
3. `extension_config::<T>()` reads `[extensions.<extension>]` as a typed value and returns explicit errors: a table that does not fit `T` is an error, never a silent default. A missing table reads as an empty table.
   - On `StartCx` it reads the server's configuration.
   - On `ActionCx` and `ProjectCx` it reads the session's effective configuration, the same one `config()` returns.
   - The extension name comes from the registration, so an extension cannot read another extension's table.
4. heca carries no heca-pro fields: `[extensions.*]` is a generic table.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: heca-pro (T013) needs an archive per server that is found again after a restart. The epoch cannot do that because it changes on every start. Two concurrent standalone windows sharing one archive would corrupt it. A typed read with explicit errors catches configuration mistakes early, and reading the session's effective configuration keeps it consistent with `config()`.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
- Data root: `heca_config::state_file::data_path` / `dirs::data_dir()`. Tests inject a temporary root.
- Slot lock: reuse the exclusive file lock pattern of the socket listener (heca/src/server/socket/listener.rs takes a lock on default.lock). Hold the lock in the ServiceHost or ServerLoop for the server's life.
- The server name is passed explicitly by the daemon entry (`headless.rs` serve) and by standalone (`client/local.rs`) into `ServerLoop::from_config`.
- `Config` gets a generic `extensions` table merged through the existing layering.

checklist.title: StartCx::data_dir — per server name + service, created owner-only, stable across restarts; server name passed by daemon (default) and standalone (standalone)
[extensions.<name>] kept in Config through the same layering; extension_config::<T>() on StartCx/ActionCx/ProjectCx scoped to the service's own extension; refreshed on reload
Tests (temp data root, restart keeps the folder, two services isolated, config layering + isolation + missing table) and docs (extending-heca.md, config.default.toml/README)
